name: xoverpi
bayer_notes: Confirmed against the hardware 2026-09-14: rpicam-hello --list-cameras reports 'ov5647 [2592x1944 10-bit GBRG]'. splay-graticule/CLAUDE.md flags OV5647-vs-IMX708 Bayer order as a RECURRING mistake (OV5647 = SGBRG10, IMX708 = SRGGB10) - do not copy an order from another camera's file.
black_level_notes: INHERITED from starcam's OV5647 and NOT verified on this sensor. starcam measured 15.30 from its own 4x coadd floor. Whether this is the same physical module moved over or a different OV5647 is unrecorded - measure before relying on it for photometry.
capture_resolution_notes: Binned 2x2 is the DEFAULT capture mode, on two independent grounds. Optically it costs nothing: the primary is spherical at f/3.95 giving ~1.1 waves P-V, ~4x the Rayleigh limit, so real star images are several arcsec wide against a 0.96 arcsec pixel. Practically it is the difference between fitting a night on the card and not - see storage below.
plate_scale_notes: THEORETICAL, not plate-solved: 206.265 * 1.4 um / 300 mm = 0.9626 arcsec/px unbinned (1.925 binned 2x2). Field of view 0.693 x 0.520 deg. REPLACE THIS from the streaks themselves: trailed stars self-calibrate, since streak length at known exposure gives plate_scale*cos(dec) and streak direction gives orientation - free on every frame, and it tracks flexure and focus drift in a way a one-off plate solve does not.
frames_root_notes: Intended to be muppet's bigstore export, automounted by the ansible nfs-client role - requested from the ansible strand 2026-09-14, NOT YET IN PLACE. Until it is, this is a local directory on the SD card and the disk guard in the daemon is the only thing preventing a full card.
night_layout_notes: night/YYYY-MM-DD/HH/<RUNTAG>-NNNN.fits.fz, Rice-compressed, written directly by the capture daemon. NOT starcam's npy layout: that existed only because the Pi 1B could not compress in-line. xoverpi is a Pi 3B (ARMv7, quad-core, 921 MB) and compresses comfortably at this cadence.
processing_host_notes: A Pi 3B can compress in-line but should not stack or plate-solve; pipeline stages run where the frames land.

exposure.notes: MEASURED on this camera via Picamera2 camera_controls, not quoted from documentation. 3066985 us is IDENTICAL across all four of {video, still} x {full-res, binned} - video mode does NOT buy a longer exposure on the OV5647. FrameDurationLimits tops out at the same 3067365 us, which is the mechanism: exposure is bounded by frame length and the driver's VBLANK ceiling does not vary by mode. An earlier note in this estate suggesting a 6 s ceiling was wrong.

storage.rice_measured_on: 2026-09-14, daylight foliage, gain 1, mean 242 max 621 of 1023 - a HIGH-entropy scene, so this ratio is a conservative worst case. Night sky is mostly empty and should compress better; re-measure on real subs.
storage.notes: This is the decisive number for the whole design. At 3 s cadence full-res fills the card in ~4.1 h - less than a night. Binned lasts ~16.4 h, which covers even a midwinter night. So binned capture is self-sufficient on local disk and the NFS mount is an improvement, not a prerequisite.

optics.type: Newtonian reflector, spherical primary, tabletop alt-az Dobsonian
optics.focus_reachable_notes: CONFIRMED 2026-09-14 by imaging a sycamore at 35 m: the sensor reaches focus at prime focus and the image circle covers the full frame with no vignetting. This was flagged as a potentially fatal unknown and is now closed. Focusing at 35 m sits f^2/(d-f) = 300^2/(35000-300) = 2.59 mm OUTSIDE the infinity position, so going from the tree to stars means racking IN 2.59 mm.
optics.ir_cut_notes: The OV5647's IR-cut filter lives in the lens assembly, which is removed to reach prime focus - so this is now a panchromatic camera. Measured on the 35 m frames: R/G 1.16-1.32 and B/G 1.06-1.10 on a foliage scene that should be strongly green-dominant, the near-IR wood effect. For a MIRROR this is close to free signal (no chromatic aberration to smear the extra band), but colour is meaningless and NIR skyglow adds background.
optics.notes: Celestron FirstScope, International Year of Astronomy 2009 edition (21024-IYA). NO tracking and NO finder - both are operational constraints on the capture design, not footnotes. The absent finder is the live obstacle to acquiring a target in a 0.69 x 0.52 deg field (1.3 x 1.0 moon diameters).

drift.notes: Alt-az, undriven, and the smear is TREATED AS SIGNAL rather than as a limit. Sidereal drift is a deterministic 1-D box convolution: direction and length are computable from geometry and exposure and are near-uniform across a 0.69 deg field, so this is KNOWN-PSF deconvolution, not blind. Trailed stars also carry astrometry.
drift.sub_length_rationale: In the read-noise-dominated regime total SNR at fixed integration time is INDEPENDENT of sub length, so sub length is a practical choice. Working range 1-3 s; the upper end is set by the MEASURED 3.07 s hardware ceiling, not by trailing.
drift.vary_sub_length: DO alternate sub exposure lengths across a stack. A box kernel's MTF is a sinc with exact nulls at n/L where information is destroyed outright; nulls for L1 do not coincide with nulls for L2, so mixed lengths fill each other's dead frequencies. Implemented: the daemon cycles XOVER_EXPOSURES.

polar_regime.notes: Near the pole the whole smear problem evaporates: Polaris drifts 88x slower than an equatorial star, so even at the 3.07 s ceiling it trails HALF A PIXEL and no deconvolution is needed. Field crossing is 4.1 hours against 166 s at the equator, so on an untracked mount the pole is the one region you can set up on once and leave - which also makes Polaris (mag 2.0) the right focus target, since it will not wander off while the focuser is being adjusted. Corollary: a 60 s coadd smears only 10.6 px near the pole against ~940 px at the equator, so eclipticam-v1's COADD_N=20 design is viable HERE and nowhere else in this setup.

drift.field_rotation: Alt-az: negligible within a sub but real across a night. Registration must solve ROTATION as well as translation, and the rate diverges near the zenith.

read_noise_todo: UNMEASURED. RN~3e- and QE~0.4 are assumed. The frame-difference of two matched darks gives RN directly. Measure before tuning gain.

state.notes: Sun-altitude gate thresholds, asymmetric for hysteresis so the boundary cannot flap. Deliberately 2 deg darker than astrocam's -10/-8: astrocam is a wide-field camera whose frames are usable through late twilight, whereas this is a 0.69 deg field of faint stars behind a 76 mm aperture, where nautical dark (-12) is the point the sky stops dominating. Gating on sun ALTITUDE rather than frame brightness follows eclipticam-v3w and astrocam: altitude is a hard physical signal, while brightness is confused by headlights, moon, AE wobble and cloud.
